judged_text: The attendee rows are committed via prisma.booking.update (line 92) before eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees runs (line 168) with no transaction and no rollback, so a calendar failure returns an error after the DB write has already persisted. If updateCalendarAttendees throws (calendar API outage, credential not valid for the referenced calendar), the user sees an error toast and keeps the dialog open believing nothing happened, but the guests are already persisted; on retry the dedupe filter removes all guests and the mutation returns the misleading BAD_REQUEST 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' instead of completing — the calendar event never gets the new attendees and the user is told the emails are invalid.

record.issue_text: [BUG] The attendee rows are committed via prisma.booking.update (line 92) before eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees runs (line 168) with no transaction and no rollback, so a calendar failure returns an error after the DB write has already persisted. If updateCalendarAttendees throws (calendar API outage, credential not valid for the referenced calendar), the user sees an error toast and keeps the dialog open believing nothing happened, but the guests are already persisted; on retry the dedupe filter removes all guests and the mutation returns the misleading BAD_REQUEST 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' instead of completing — the calendar event never gets the new attendees and the user is told the emails are invalid.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the DB write happens via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` before `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` is called, and there is no transaction/rollback around these steps. Since `updateCalendarAttendees` is not wrapped in a try/catch (only email sending is), any calendar/API failure will throw after the attendees have already been persisted. On the client, `onSuccess` is the only place that closes the dialog/resets state, so an error leaves the dialog open implying nothing changed. A retry will fetch the booking with the newly persisted attendees and `uniqueGuests` becomes empty (filtered out by `booking.attendees.some(...)`), causing a `BAD_REQUEST` with message `emails_must_be_unique_valid`, matching the described misleading behavior and leaving the external calendar unsynced.
